title: Purpose, reason and means
summary: Formal ways to express purpose ({んがため}, {べく}), cause ({ゆえに}, {ばこそ}, {こととて}), pretexts ({にかこつけて}), means and formal end points ({をもって}), and acting to save face ({手前[てまえ]}).

points.title: 〜んがため(に)
points.meaning: in order to; for the sake of (with strong determination)
points.structure: Verb ない-stem + んがため(に) / んがための + Noun (する → せんがため)
points.explanation:
{〜んがため} is built from the classical volitional {ん} ('intend to') plus {がため} ('for the purpose of'). It means 'with the firm aim of doing X' and usually describes someone making great sacrifices or efforts for a goal.

Conjugation: take the nai-stem and add {んがため}: {勝[か]つ} → {勝[か]たんがため}, {生[い]きる} → {生[い]きんがため}. {する} becomes {せんがため}.

**Register:** literary and very formal — novels, historical writing, speeches, editorials. Not used in conversation; there you'd say {〜ために}.

examples.jp: 生[い]きんがために、人々[ひとびと]は必死[ひっし]で働[はたら]いた。
examples.en: People worked desperately just to survive.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は夢[ゆめ]を実現[じつげん]せんがため、全[すべ]てを犠牲[ぎせい]にした。
examples.en: He sacrificed everything to make his dream come true.

examples.jp: 真実[しんじつ]を明[あき]らかにせんがための調査[ちょうさ]が続[つづ]けられている。
examples.en: An investigation aimed at uncovering the truth is continuing.

examples.jp: 勝[か]たんがためには手段[しゅだん]を選[えら]ばないという姿勢[しせい]には、疑問[ぎもん]を感[かん]じる。
examples.en: I have doubts about an attitude of doing whatever it takes just to win.

points.notes: Not for everyday purposes like {✕パンを買[か]わんがためにコンビニへ行[い]った}. It needs a weighty goal.

quiz.q: 彼[かれ]は試合[しあい]に勝[か]た＿＿、毎日[まいにち]厳[きび]しい練習[れんしゅう]を続[つづ]けた。
quiz.en: Determined to win the match, he kept up harsh training every day.

quiz.q: 会社[かいしゃ]は利益[りえき]を上[あ]げ＿＿ため、従業員[じゅうぎょういん]の安全[あんぜん]を軽視[けいし]していた。
quiz.en: In its drive to make a profit, the company had neglected the safety of its workers.

points.title: 〜べく
points.meaning: in order to; with the aim of
points.structure: Verb (dictionary form) + べく (する → すべく／するべく)
points.explanation:
{べく} is the continuative form of {べし} (see Unit 14). {〜べく} means 'in order to do X' and shows a deliberate purpose. It is much more common than {んがため}, especially in the news: companies act {〜すべく}, committees are set up {〜すべく}, volunteers gather {〜すべく}.

The second half is a concrete action taken to achieve the goal.

**Register:** formal and written; frequent in news, business reports and press releases. Also heard in formal speeches.

examples.jp: 被災地[ひさいち]を支援[しえん]すべく、多[おお]くのボランティアが集[あつ]まった。
examples.en: Many volunteers gathered to support the disaster-hit area.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は弁護士[べんごし]になるべく、毎日[まいにち]十時間[じゅうじかん]勉強[べんきょう]している。
examples.en: He studies ten hours a day with the aim of becoming a lawyer.

examples.jp: 真相[しんそう]を究明[きゅうめい]すべく、調査[ちょうさ]委員会[いいんかい]が設置[せっち]された。
examples.en: An investigative committee was set up to get to the bottom of the matter.

examples.jp: 同社[どうしゃ]は海外[かいがい]市場[しじょう]に進出[しんしゅつ]すべく、現地[げんち]企業[きぎょう]との提携[ていけい]を進[すす]めている。
examples.en: The company is pursuing partnerships with local firms in order to expand into overseas markets.

points.notes: Related forms: {〜べくして} 'as was bound to happen' ({起[お]こるべくして起[お]こった事故[じこ]}) and {〜べくもない} 'there's no way to' ({知[し]るべくもない}). Not for requests or commands in the second half.

quiz.q: 留学[りゅうがく]の費用[ひよう]を貯[た]める＿＿、彼女[かのじょ]はアルバイトを三[みっ]つ掛[か]け持[も]ちしている。
quiz.en: To save money for studying abroad, she's working three part-time jobs.

quiz.q: 事故[じこ]の原因[げんいん]を明[あき]らかに＿＿、専門家[せんもんか]による調査[ちょうさ]が始[はじ]まった。
quiz.en: An investigation by experts has begun in order to determine the cause of the accident.

points.title: 〜ゆえ(に)／〜がゆえに
points.structure: Noun (の) + ゆえ(に) / plain form + (が)ゆえに / Noun + ゆえの + Noun
points.explanation:
{ゆえ} ({故[ゆえ]}) is a classical word for 'reason'. {〜ゆえ(に)} means 'because of X' and sounds logical, weighty or literary. {〜がゆえに} after a clause is common in essays: {不便[ふべん]であるがゆえに} 'precisely because it is inconvenient'.

As a sentence connector, {ゆえに} means 'therefore' — used in logic and mathematics. And Descartes' famous line is {我[われ]思[おも]う、ゆえに我[われ]あり} 'I think, therefore I am'.

**Register:** written, academic and literary. {若[わか]さゆえの過[あやま]ち} 'a mistake of youth' is a well-known phrase.

examples.jp: 若[わか]さゆえの過[あやま]ちは、誰[だれ]にでもある。
examples.en: Everyone makes mistakes because they're young.

examples.jp: 我[われ]思[おも]う、ゆえに我[われ]あり。
examples.en: I think, therefore I am.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は貧[まず]しさゆえに、学校[がっこう]に通[かよ]うことができなかった。
examples.en: Because of poverty, he was unable to attend school.

examples.jp: この地域[ちいき]は交通[こうつう]が不便[ふべん]であるがゆえに、若者[わかもの]の流出[りゅうしゅつ]が続[つづ]いている。
examples.en: Because transport in this region is so inconvenient, young people keep leaving.

points.notes: In conversation, use {〜から} or {〜ので}. {〜ゆえ} without {に} is even more literary.

quiz.q: 彼女[かのじょ]は正直[しょうじき]すぎる＿＿、時々[ときどき]人[ひと]を傷[きず]つけてしまう。
quiz.en: Because she's too honest, she sometimes ends up hurting people.

quiz.q: 子[こ]どもを思[おも]う＿＿の厳[きび]しさだということは、大人[おとな]になってから分[わ]かった。
quiz.en: It was only after I grew up that I understood that the strictness came from caring about the child.

points.title: 〜ばこそ
points.meaning: precisely because; it is only because
points.structure: Verb / Adjective ば-form + こそ (Noun / な-adj + であればこそ)
points.explanation:
{〜ばこそ} is an emphatic 'because'. It insists that X is the true reason — often a reason the listener may not have realised. 'I say harsh things *because* I care about you.'

It usually explains a positive motive behind something that might look negative (strictness, criticism, sacrifice), or highlights an essential precondition. The sentence often ends in {〜のだ}.

**Register:** formal and slightly literary, but used in heartfelt speech. Similar in meaning to {〜からこそ}, which is far more common in conversation.

examples.jp: あなたのことを思[おも]えばこそ、厳[きび]しいことを言[い]うのです。
examples.en: It's precisely because I care about you that I'm being harsh.

examples.jp: 健康[けんこう]であればこそ、好[す]きな仕事[しごと]を続[つづ]けられる。
examples.en: It's only because I'm healthy that I can keep doing the work I love.

examples.jp: 家族[かぞく]の支[ささ]えがあればこそ、ここまで頑張[がんば]ってこられた。
examples.en: It's only because of my family's support that I've been able to keep going this far.

examples.jp: 信頼[しんらい]していればこそ、彼[かれ]に大事[だいじ]な仕事[しごと]を任[まか]せたのだ。
examples.en: It's precisely because I trust him that I entrusted him with such important work.

points.notes: Not used for negative reasons: {✕寝坊[ねぼう]すればこそ遅刻[ちこく]した}. Use {〜からこそ} in everyday talk.

quiz.q: 君[きみ]に期待[きたい]して＿＿、こうして注意[ちゅうい]しているんだ。
quiz.en: It's precisely because I have high hopes for you that I'm warning you like this.

quiz.q: 愛[あい]して＿＿、別[わか]れを選[えら]んだのだ。
quiz.en: It was precisely because I loved her that I chose to part.

points.title: 〜こととて
points.meaning: because; since (as an excuse or apology)
points.structure: Verb / Adjective (plain) + こととて / Noun + の + こととて
points.explanation:
{〜こととて} gives a reason, usually as an excuse when apologising or asking for forgiveness: 'Since it was my first time, please forgive any shortcomings.' 'Since it was done by a child, please let it go.'

It can also simply state a circumstance: {休日[きゅうじつ]のこととて} 'it being a holiday'. A typical lead-in is {何分[なにぶん]} 'after all, you see'.

**Register:** old-fashioned and very formal; seen in letters, formal apologies and historical novels. You'll rarely hear it today, but it appears on the JLPT and in very polite business apologies.

examples.jp: 慣[な]れないこととて、ご迷惑[めいわく]をおかけしました。
examples.en: I'm sorry for the trouble; I'm not used to this.

examples.jp: 子[こ]どものしたこととて、どうか許[ゆる]してやってください。
examples.en: It was done by a child, so please forgive him.

examples.jp: 休日[きゅうじつ]のこととて、役所[やくしょ]はどこも閉[し]まっていた。
examples.en: It being a holiday, all the government offices were closed.

examples.jp: 何分[なにぶん]初[はじ]めてのこととて、至[いた]らない点[てん]もあるかと存[ぞん]じます。
examples.en: As this is, after all, my first time, I expect there will be some shortcomings.

points.notes: Don't confuse it with {〜とて} 'even' ({子[こ]どもとて容赦[ようしゃ]しない} 'won't show mercy even to a child').

quiz.q: 不慣[ふな]れな＿＿、手続[てつづ]きに時間[じかん]がかかってしまい申[もう]し訳[わけ]ありません。
quiz.en: I'm sorry the procedure took so long; I'm not used to it.

quiz.q: 何[なに]しろ急[きゅう]な＿＿、十分[じゅうぶん]な準備[じゅんび]ができませんでした。
quiz.en: As it was so sudden, we couldn't prepare sufficiently.

points.title: 〜にかこつけて
points.meaning: using X as an excuse / pretext
points.explanation:
{かこつける} means 'to use as a pretext'. {X にかこつけて Y} means 'using X as an excuse, someone does Y (what they really wanted to do)'. Dad goes out drinking every night 'for work socialising'; someone goes sightseeing 'on a business trip'.

The tone is critical or self-mocking: the stated reason isn't the real one.

**Register:** neutral; used in conversation and writing. Fairly common in real life, especially when teasing someone.

examples.jp: 出張[しゅっちょう]にかこつけて、観光[かんこう]を楽[たの]しんできた。
examples.en: I used the business trip as an excuse to do some sightseeing.

examples.jp: 父[ちち]は付[つ]き合[あ]いにかこつけて、毎晩[まいばん]飲[の]みに行[い]く。
examples.en: My father goes drinking every night under the pretext of socialising for work.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は体調[たいちょう]不良[ふりょう]にかこつけて、面倒[めんどう]な会議[かいぎ]を欠席[けっせき]した。
examples.en: He used feeling unwell as an excuse to skip the tedious meeting.

examples.jp: 子[こ]どもの誕生日[たんじょうび]にかこつけて、自分[じぶん]が欲[ほ]しかったゲームを買[か]った。
examples.en: Using my child's birthday as an excuse, I bought a game I'd wanted myself.

points.notes: Similar: {〜を口実[こうじつ]に} 'using X as a pretext'. {かこつけて} implies the excuse is thin.

quiz.q: 彼[かれ]は仕事[しごと]が忙[いそが]しいこと＿＿、家事[かじ]を全[まった]く手伝[てつだ]わない。
quiz.en: Using his busy job as an excuse, he doesn't help with the housework at all.

quiz.q: 打[う]ち合[あ]わせ＿＿、取引先[とりひきさき]の近[ちか]くの有名[ゆうめい]なラーメン屋[や]に行[い]ってきた。
quiz.en: Using the client meeting as an excuse, I went to a famous ramen shop near their office.

points.title: 〜をもって
points.meaning: (1) by means of; with; (2) as of (formal end point)
points.structure: Noun + をもって / をもちまして (more polite) / をもってすれば
points.explanation:
{〜をもって} is a formal particle with two main uses:

**1. Means or method:** 'by means of, with' — {書面[しょめん]をもって} 'in writing', {身[み]をもって} 'personally, first-hand', {実力[じつりょく]をもってすれば} 'with (his) ability, (anything is possible)'.

**2. Time limit / end point:** 'as of, with X (it ends)' — {本日[ほんじつ]をもちまして閉店[へいてん]いたします} 'we close as of today'; {以上[いじょう]をもちまして} 'with that, (we conclude)'.

**Register:** very formal. Use 2 is everywhere in Japanese working life: meeting chairs say {以上[いじょう]をもちまして、本日[ほんじつ]の会議[かいぎ]を終了[しゅうりょう]いたします}, and shops post closure notices with it. Worth knowing actively.

examples.jp: 以上[いじょう]をもちまして、本日[ほんじつ]の会議[かいぎ]を終了[しゅうりょう]いたします。
examples.en: With that, we conclude today's meeting.

examples.jp: 試験[しけん]の結果[けっか]は、書面[しょめん]をもってお知[し]らせします。
examples.en: You will be notified of the exam results in writing.

examples.jp: 本日[ほんじつ]をもちまして、当店[とうてん]は閉店[へいてん]いたします。
examples.en: As of today, this shop will be closing.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]の実力[じつりょく]をもってすれば、優勝[ゆうしょう]も夢[ゆめ]ではない。
examples.en: With his ability, winning the championship isn't just a dream.

points.notes: {〜を限[かぎ]りに} (Unit 1) is similar to use 2 but emphasises 'this is the last time'; {〜をもって} is the more official, neutral announcement.

quiz.q: 合否[ごうひ]の結果[けっか]は、メール＿＿ご連絡[れんらく]いたします。
quiz.en: We will notify you by email of whether you passed or failed.

quiz.q: 三月[さんがつ]三十一日[さんじゅういちにち]＿＿、本[ほん]サービスの提供[ていきょう]を終了[しゅうりょう]いたします。
quiz.en: As of March 31, we will discontinue this service.

points.title: 〜手前[てまえ]
points.meaning: because of (one's position / what one has said); in front of (so as not to lose face)
points.structure: Verb (plain, often た-form) + 手前[てまえ] / Noun + の + 手前[てまえ]
points.explanation:
{手前[てまえ]} literally means 'in front of oneself'. As grammar, it describes a constraint of face: because of what you've said or done, or because certain people are watching, you can't act a certain way. 'Having boasted that I'd win, I can't lose now.' 'In front of my kids, I can't break my promise.'

The second half is usually {〜わけにはいかない}, {〜なければならない} or {〜とは言[い]えない}.

**Register:** neutral to slightly formal; genuinely used in conversation. Very relevant to Japanese social life, where saving face matters.

examples.jp: 子[こ]どもの手前[てまえ]、親[おや]が約束[やくそく]を破[やぶ]るわけにはいかない。
examples.en: In front of the children, parents can't break their promises.

examples.jp: 大口[おおぐち]をたたいた手前[てまえ]、負[ま]けるわけにはいかない。
examples.en: After all my big talk, I can't afford to lose.

examples.jp: 部下[ぶか]の手前[てまえ]、上司[じょうし]として弱音[よわね]を吐[は]くわけにはいかない。
examples.en: With my subordinates watching, I can't complain as their boss.

examples.jp: 「必[かなら]ず成功[せいこう]させる」と言[い]ってしまった手前[てまえ]、今更[いまさら]やめるとは言[い]えない。
examples.en: Having said 'I'll definitely make it succeed', I can't say I'm quitting now.

points.notes: {手前[てまえ]} also simply means 'just before (a place)': {駅[えき]の手前[てまえ]} 'just before the station'. Context makes it clear.

quiz.q: みんなの前[まえ]で「絶対[ぜったい]に合格[ごうかく]する」と宣言[せんげん]した＿＿、落[お]ちるわけにはいかない。
quiz.en: Having declared in front of everyone that I'll definitely pass, I can't fail.

quiz.q: 後輩[こうはい]の＿＿、先輩[せんぱい]の私[わたし]が泣[な]き言[ごと]を言[い]うわけにはいかない。
quiz.en: With my juniors watching, I, as their senior, can't go whining.
